claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions about your circumstances. Let me start with the basics:

Do you have any children that you're responsible for?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I do. I have a son, Alex. He's 17 and lives at home with me. I wanted to check if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.

Let me ask you a few questions about Alex's situation:

Is Alex currently in approved education or training (such as school, college, or an approved training program)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he is. Alex is still in college doing his A-levels.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful to know. Now I need to understand a bit more about the timing:

When did Alex turn 16, or when will he turn 16?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Oh, he's already 17 now, so he turned 16 last year.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. To help determine his eligibility, I need to know:

What date specifically did Alex turn 16? (The exact date, or at least the month and year would be helpful)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hmm, let me think... he turned 16 last year in March. So that would be March 2024.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Now I need to clarify the details of his education:

Is Alex enrolled in full-time approved education (which typically means more than 12 hours per week of supervised study), and is this education considered "non-advanced" (such as A-levels, rather than university-level study)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right. He's doing full-time A-levels at the local sixth form college. It's definitely more than 12 hours a week - he's there all day during the week.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, that's very helpful. I have just a couple more questions:

1. Are you the person responsible for Alex - meaning, does he live with you and are you responsible for his care and upbringing?

2. Are you currently living in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes to both. Alex lives at home with me, and yes, I live in the UK - we're in Manchester.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great news! **You are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Here's why: Alex meets all the necessary criteria:
- He is 17 years old (under 20)
- He is in full-time, non-advanced education (A-levels at sixth form college)
- He lives with you and you're responsible for him
- You're living in the UK

Under UK Child Benefit rules, you can claim for children aged 16-19 who are in approved full-time education or training. A-levels are considered non-advanced education, and since Alex is attending full-time (more than 12 hours per week of supervised study), he qualifies.

You should be able to claim Child Benefit for Alex until he either:
- Turns 20, or
- Leaves full-time education (whichever comes first)

If you haven't already claimed, you can apply for Child Benefit through the government website or by post. Is there anything else you'd like to know about your Child Benefit eligibility?

reasonings: Alex is currently 17 years old (turned 16 in March 2024) and is enrolled in full-time, non-advanced education (A-levels at sixth form college). Under UK Child Benefit rules, you can claim Child Benefit for a child aged 16-19 if they are in approved full-time education or training that is non-advanced (such as A-levels). Alex meets these criteria as he is: (1) under 20 years old, (2) in full-time education (more than 12 hours per week of supervised study), (3) studying a non-advanced qualification (A-levels), and (4) living with the claimant who is responsible for him. The claimant is also living in the UK. Therefore, Alex qualifies for Child Benefit.
